title: Fixed Wide Head and Trunnion Pedestal Viewer
description: One newly authored complete fixed public-viewing-instrument exterior. A single broad closed shouldered head casing contains the back walls of two genuinely deep front circular blind recesses and two smaller rear eyecups. The single connected wide head is not a pair of imported handheld binocular bodies or a telescope tube. A continuous transverse axle carries the head inside one whole open U-shaped fork, leaving real side and under-head gaps. The fork is seated on a thick vertical pedestal with one complete broad circular grounded foot; a whole rear arched grasp frame has two embedded roots and a visible hand opening behind the casing. All coordinates authored for this entire mounted object. Unlike the old handheld binoculars there is no open central bridge between separate prism barrels; unlike the three-foot single-tube telescope there is no long tube, tripod or mounting collar. Three opaque constant PBR roles, metre units Z up, whole horizontal bounds-centred ground datum; one model zero scenes. Empty fixed visual instrument only: no transparent optics, magnification, focus, view generation, turning mechanism, coin/payment system, electrical supply, person fit, handling, installation, load or public-use safety capability. Rigging animation interaction not made.
